Alabama.waitRule: Alabama bars cremation within 24 hours of death unless a medical examiner waives it for infectious disease; the authorizing agent must sign the consent.

regulator.org: Alabama Board of Funeral Services

stateCems.name: Alabama State Veterans Memorial Cemetery at Spanish Fort

Alabama.cremationNote: Alabama does not make families hire a funeral director for every arrangement, but every cremation must be arranged through a funeral establishment licensed by the Alabama Board of Funeral Services (Ala. Code § 34-13-121(b)).

Alaska.waitRule: Alaska sets no waiting period before cremation. The person with the right to control disposition must authorize it, and a burial-transit permit is required.

regulator.org: Alaska Division of Corporations, Business and Professional Licensing (mortuary science program)

Arizona.waitRule: Arizona has no waiting period before cremation. The authorizing agent must give prior written consent and the medical examiner reviews the death certificate.

regulator.org: Arizona Department of Health Services, Bureau of Licensing for Professions & Occupations (BLPO)

stateCems.name: Arizona Veterans Memorial Cemetery at Camp Navajo
Arizona Veterans Memorial Cemetery at Marana

Arkansas.waitRule: Arkansas has no waiting period before cremation. A cremation authorization signed by the authorizing agent and a death certificate are required.

regulator.org: Arkansas Insurance Department, Funeral Services Division

stateCems.name: Arkansas State Veterans Cemetery at Birdeye
Arkansas State Veterans Cemetery at North Little Rock

California.waitRule: California has no waiting period before cremation, but requires a filed death certificate, a permit for disposition and written authorization.

regulator.org: California Cemetery and Funeral Bureau

aid.text: California counties handle indigent burial or cremation under Health & Safety Code § 7104; the county coroner or public administrator can explain the local process.
aid.contact: the county coroner or public administrator

Colorado.waitRule: Colorado lets families arrange cremation without a funeral director. There is no waiting period, but the crematory needs written authorization.

regulator.org: Colorado Department of Regulatory Agencies

stateCems.name: Veterans Memorial Cemetery of Western Colorado

Connecticut.waitRule: Connecticut requires a 48-hour waiting period before cremation unless death was from a communicable disease, plus a medical examiner's certificate.

regulator.org: Connecticut Department of Public Health

fdRestricted: filing the death certificate, moving the body, and obtaining the disposition permit

aid.text: The Connecticut Department of Social Services funeral and burial allowance pays up to $1,800; contributions over $3,400 reduce it, and you must apply within one year. Medicaid applicants may set aside up to $10,000 in an irrevocable funeral contract (Conn. Gen. Stat. § 42-207).
aid.contact: the Connecticut Department of Social Services

Delaware.waitRule: Delaware has no waiting period, but a body may be cremated only under a permit signed by the chief medical examiner, with next-of-kin authorization.

regulator.org: Delaware Division of Professional Regulation

stateCems.name: Delaware Veterans Memorial Cemetery - New Castle County
Delaware Veterans Memorial Cemetery - Sussex County

District of Columbia.waitRule: The District has no waiting period. A funeral director needs next-of-kin authorization, a filed death certificate, a Registrar's permit and medical examiner approval.

regulator.org: DC Occupational and Professional Licensing Administration

Florida.waitRule: Florida law bars cremation until 48 hours after death; the district medical examiner must also approve it first.

regulator.org: Florida Department of Financial Services

Georgia.waitRule: Georgia sets no waiting period before cremation, but a disposition permit from the local registrar is required.

regulator.org: Georgia State Board of Funeral Service

Hawaii.waitRule: Hawaii sets no waiting period before cremation; a health department permit is required and cannot issue until a death certificate is filed.

regulator.org: Hawaii Department of Health

national.name: National Memorial Cemetery of the Pacific

Idaho.waitRule: Idaho sets no waiting period, but the coroner of the county where the death occurred must give written authorization to cremate.

regulator.org: Idaho Division of Occupational and Professional Licenses

stateCems.name: Idaho State Veterans Cemetery at Blackfoot
Idaho State Veterans Cemetery at Boise

Illinois.waitRule: Illinois bars cremation within 24 hours of death and requires a cremation permit from the county coroner or medical examiner plus a signed authorization form.

regulator.org: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

fdRestricted: filing the death certificate, moving the body, being present at burial or cremation, and obtaining permits

aid.text: The Illinois Department of Human Services pays up to $1,370 toward funeral services and $686 toward burial or cremation (up to $2,056) for eligible recipients; the claim must be filed within 180 days of death.
aid.contact: the Illinois Department of Human Services

Indiana.waitRule: Indiana bars cremation less than 48 hours after death unless the city or county health officer waives it in writing; an authorizing agent must sign.

regulator.org: Indiana Professional Licensing Agency

aid.text: Indiana FSSA can pay up to $1,200 for the funeral and $800 for the cemetery for eligible Medicaid recipients; the claim must be filed within 90 days (Ind. Code § 12-14-17).
aid.contact: your local FSSA Division of Family Resources office

Iowa.waitRule: Iowa sets no waiting period before cremation, but a county or state medical examiner must first issue a cremation permit.

regulator.org: Iowa Department of Inspections, Appeals, and Licensing

Kansas.waitRule: Kansas sets no mandatory waiting period, but a crematory needs a signed authorization form and a coroner's permit to cremate.

regulator.org: Kansas State Board of Mortuary Arts

stateCems.name: Kansas Veterans Cemetery at Fort Dodge
Kansas Veterans Cemetery at Fort Riley / Manhattan

Kentucky.waitRule: Kentucky sets no waiting period, but cremation requires a coroner's permit and a filed provisional death certificate first.

regulator.org: Kentucky Board of Embalmers and Funeral Directors

Louisiana.waitRule: Louisiana sets no waiting period before cremation: a funeral director arranges it on the next of kin's signed authorization, and the coroner issues the permit.

regulator.org: Louisiana State Board of Embalmers and Funeral Directors

fdRestricted: filing the death certificate, moving the body, and being present at the final disposition

Maine.waitRule: Maine bars cremation within 48 hours of death unless a contagious disease caused it, and a medical examiner must certify the death first.

regulator.org: Maine Board of Funeral Service

stateCems.name: Houlton Band of Maliseet Indians Veterans Cemetery

Maryland.waitRule: Maryland bars cremation until at least 12 hours after death, and requires written authorization from the legal next of kin; no medical examiner sign-off.

regulator.org: Maryland Department of Health

Massachusetts.waitRule: Massachusetts bars cremation within 48 hours of death unless a contagious disease caused it, and a medical examiner must view the body and authorize it.

regulator.org: Massachusetts Board of Embalming and Funeral Directing

aid.text: The Massachusetts Department of Transitional Assistance pays up to $1,100 toward a funeral for eligible people, but only when the total cost is no more than $3,500.

Michigan.waitRule: Michigan sets no waiting period before cremation, but the medical examiner of the county where the death occurred must sign the authorization.

regulator.org: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs

fdRestricted: filing the death certificate, moving the body, supervising the disposition, and obtaining permits

aid.text: Michigan State Emergency Relief (SER) burial payments for 2026 are $875 for burial with a memorial service, $610 without, $640 for cremation with a memorial, and $390 without.

Minnesota.waitRule: Minnesota sets no waiting period; it requires written authorization from whoever controls disposition, and cremation within 24 hours of custody.

regulator.org: Minnesota Department of Health, Health Regulation Division

aid.text: Minnesota counties must pay for the burial or cremation of people who die without the means to cover it (Minn. Stat. § 261.035); amounts are set by each county.

stateCems.name: Leech Lake Veterans Cemetery - Cass Lake
Minnesota State Veterans Cemetery - Little Falls

Mississippi.waitRule: Mississippi sets no waiting period, but the death certificate must be completed and filed with Vital Records before cremation.

regulator.org: Mississippi State Board of Funeral Service

Missouri.waitRule: Missouri sets no firm waiting period; written authorization to cremate from the next of kin, the coroner or the decedent is required.

regulator.org: Missouri State Board of Embalmers & Funeral Directors

stateCems.name: Missouri State Veterans Cemetery - Fort Leonard Wood

Montana.waitRule: Montana bars cremation within 24 hours of death and requires a signed cremation authorization, though no funeral director is required by law.

regulator.org: Montana Department of Labor and Industry

stateCems.name: Eastern Montana State Veterans Cemetery - Miles City
Montana State Veterans Cemetery - Fort Harrison

Nebraska.waitRule: Nebraska has no statutory waiting period, but the county attorney must sign a cremation permit and the next of kin must authorize it.

regulator.org: Nebraska Board of Funeral Directing and Embalming

fdRestricted: filing the death certificate, moving the body, obtaining permits, supervising a home burial, and arranging a cremation

stateCems.name: Nebraska Veterans Cemetery at Grand Island

Nevada.waitRule: Nevada has no statutory waiting period before cremation; the crematory needs a signed death certificate and written authorization from the authorizing agent.

regulator.org: Nevada Funeral and Cemetery Services Board

New Hampshire.waitRule: New Hampshire bars cremation within 48 hours of death unless death was from a contagious disease, and requires a medical examiner's certificate.

regulator.org: New Hampshire Office of Professional Licensure and Certification

New Jersey.waitRule: New Jersey requires at least 24 hours to elapse after death before cremation, and cremating without a final disposition permit is a crime.

regulator.org: New Jersey Division of Consumer Affairs

fdRestricted: filing the death certificate, moving the body, and being present at the final disposition

aid.text: New Jersey WorkFirst/General Assistance can pay up to $3,056 for the funeral and $714 for the cemetery ($3,770 total); family contributions up to $1,570 do not reduce it (N.J.A.C. 10:90-8.5).

stateCems.name: Brigadier General William C. Doyle Veterans Memorial Cemetery

New Mexico.waitRule: New Mexico sets no waiting period, but no cremation may occur without signed authorization and a permit from the Office of the Medical Investigator.

regulator.org: New Mexico Board of Funeral Services

New York.waitRule: New York has no statutory waiting period; cremation requires a disposition permit and an authorization form signed by the next of kin.

regulator.org: New York State Department of Health, Bureau of Funeral Directing

fdRestricted: filing the death certificate, moving the body, obtaining the permit, and supervising the disposition

aid.text: In New York each county social-services district sets its own burial-assistance rules; in New York City, HRA pays up to $1,700 and the total bill generally cannot exceed $3,400.
aid.contact: the local social-services district (HRA in New York City)

national.name: Gerald B. H. Solomon Saratoga National Cemetery

stateCems.name: New York State Veterans Cemetery - Finger Lakes

North Carolina.waitRule: North Carolina bars cremation within 24 hours after death, and a medical examiner must certify that no further examination is needed.

regulator.org: North Carolina Board of Funeral Service

North Dakota.waitRule: North Dakota sets no waiting period before cremation; a final disposition-transit permit and a cremation authorization signed by the next of kin are required.

regulator.org: North Dakota State Board of Funeral Service

stateCems.name: All Nations Veterans Cemetery - Fort Yates

Ohio.waitRule: Ohio bars cremation until 24 hours after death and requires a complete death certificate, a burial-transit permit, and the next of kin's written authorization.

regulator.org: Ohio Board of Embalmers and Funeral Directors

aid.text: Under Ohio Rev. Code § 9.15, the township or city where a person lived pays for burial or cremation when the body is unclaimed or is claimed by someone with income at or below 150% of the federal poverty line, and the Ohio Board of Embalmers and Funeral Directors can reimburse that local government up to $1,000 for an adult or $750 for a child age 11 or younger, while program funds last.
aid.source: Ohio Rev. Code § 9.15; Ohio Admin. Code 4717-17-06
aid.contact: the township or city fiscal officer

Oklahoma.waitRule: Oklahoma sets no waiting period, but the medical examiner must issue a cremation permit and the next of kin must authorize the cremation in writing.

regulator.org: Oklahoma Funeral Board

stateCems.name: Seaman First Class Billy Turner Veterans Cemetery
Seminole Nation and Veterans Memorial Cemetery

Oregon.waitRule: Oregon sets no waiting period before cremation, but the medical certifier or medical examiner must authorize final disposition and a disposition permit is required.

regulator.org: Oregon Mortuary and Cemetery Board

Pennsylvania.waitRule: Pennsylvania bars cremation until 24 hours after death; the county coroner must authorize it and the next of kin holds sole authority to consent.

regulator.org: Pennsylvania State Board of Funeral Directors

aid.text: Pennsylvania DHS pays up to $750 toward burial or cremation for eligible people, paid to an enrolled funeral director; resources of $1,500 or more disqualify the estate (55 Pa. Code ch. 283).

stateCems.name: Pennsylvania Soldiers' and Sailors' Home Cemetery

Rhode Island.waitRule: Rhode Island bars cremation until 24 hours after death and requires a burial permit plus a cremation certificate from the state medical examiners.

regulator.org: Rhode Island Department of Health, Board of Funeral Directing/Embalming

South Carolina.waitRule: South Carolina bars cremation until 24 hours after death and requires a death certificate, next-of-kin authorization, and a coroner's cremation permit.

regulator.org: South Carolina Board of Funeral Service

South Dakota.waitRule: South Dakota bars cremation until 24 hours after death and requires a signed cremation authorization plus a permit for disposition.

regulator.org: South Dakota State Board of Funeral Service

stateCems.name: Akicita Owicahe Lakota Freedom Veterans Cemetery

Tennessee.waitRule: Tennessee sets no fixed waiting period before cremation, but a permit for cremation authorized by the county medical examiner is required.

regulator.org: Tennessee Board of Funeral Directors and Embalmers

stateCems.name: Tennessee State Veterans Cemetery at Parkers Crossroads

Texas.waitRule: Texas requires a 48-hour waiting period before cremation unless waived in writing by a justice of the peace, medical examiner, or court order.

regulator.org: Texas Funeral Service Commission

aid.text: Texas law makes each county commissioners court responsible for disposing of the body of a person whose family cannot pay (Tex. Health & Safety Code § 694.002); ask the county indigent-services office.
aid.contact: the county commissioners court or county indigent-services office

stateCems.name: Central Texas State Veterans Cemetery in Killeen
Coastal Bend State Veterans Cemetery in Corpus Christi
Rio Grande Valley State Veterans Cemetery in Mission

Utah.waitRule: Utah sets no waiting period before cremation; the crematory must file the death certificate and obtain the medical examiner's permit.

regulator.org: Utah Board of Funeral Service

stateCems.name: Utah Veterans Cemetery and Memorial Park

Vermont.waitRule: Vermont requires a 24-hour waiting period before cremation plus a medical examiner's certificate, though families may act without a funeral director.

regulator.org: Vermont Office of Professional Regulation

Virginia.waitRule: Virginia sets no waiting period, but the Office of the Chief Medical Examiner must authorize every cremation and next of kin must identify the body.

regulator.org: Virginia Board of Funeral Directors and Embalmers

stateCems.name: Albert G. Horton, Jr. Memorial Veterans Cemetery

Washington.waitRule: Washington sets no waiting period before cremation; families may act without a funeral director once the death is registered and a burial-transit permit issued.

regulator.org: Washington State Department of Licensing

stateCems.name: Washington State Veterans Cemetery - Medical Lake

West Virginia.waitRule: West Virginia sets no waiting period; a crematory needs written next-of-kin permission plus a medical examiner's or coroner's cremation permit.

regulator.org: West Virginia Board of Funeral Service Examiners

stateCems.name: Donel C. Kinnard Memorial State Veterans Cemetery

Wisconsin.waitRule: Wisconsin requires a 48-hour waiting period before cremation unless death was from a contagious disease, plus a coroner's or medical examiner's permit.

regulator.org: Wisconsin Department of Safety and Professional Services

aid.text: The Wisconsin Funeral and Cemetery Aids Program (WFCAP) pays up to $1,500 for funeral and up to $1,000 for cemetery or crematory costs, with limits on the total bill.
aid.contact: the county or tribal agency that handles WFCAP

Wyoming.waitRule: Wyoming has no statutory waiting period, but board rules bar cremation within 24 hours of death without the county coroner's written permission.

regulator.org: Wyoming State Board of Funeral Service Practitioners
